about: Surviving Stryker mutants individually justified as equivalent (no input changes any observable result) or unreachable, ONE ENTRY PER MUTATION SITE. Checked by tools/pca-audit/stryker/check-equivalents.mjs. Keyed by package, file, mutator, original text, replacement, trimmed source line and occurrence (which copy of that line text in the file); lineno is a hint only and multiplicity covers the same mutant reported more than once on one line.
also_audited_note: Packages in the Stryker plan (.github/scripts/ts-stryker-plan.mjs) that have no equivalent-mutant entries yet: their survivors must be killed by tests or listed here with a reason; the merge job fails on an unlisted survivor. A package with entries is in the plan by that alone.

The compile check is dead: validateWhen only reaches it after isSafeRegexSource(src) accepted, and that guard ends in compileSafeRegex(src) !== null. The linear-time parser admits only: literals, `.`, classes whose ranges it checks are ordered, the escapes d D w W s S t n v f r 0 xHH uHHHH cX and escaped punctuation (no octal, backreference, \k, \p, \b, \B), balanced (...) and (?:...) groups, `|`, quantifiers * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} with m >= n and at most one lazy `?`, never on an assertion or another quantifier, and ^ $. Each of these is also a production of the ECMAScript (Annex B, no u/v flag) pattern grammar, and none of the early errors V8 raises (out-of-order range or quantifier, invalid group name, dangling group, quantified lookaround, invalid escape) can arise from them; wrapping in ^(?: )$ keeps the group balanced because the parser required src itself to be balanced. Checked differentially, not only argued: src/regex-guard-compiles.test.ts asserts guard-accepts implies new RegExp compiles over 300k seeded token-grammar sources and the edge list (6M run once, no counterexample).
